t: A kingdom at the Shashe–Limpopo confluence whose rulers moved onto Mapungubwe Hill around 1220, apart from the commoners living below.
It grew rich on cattle and on ivory and gold traded to the coast, and buried its elite with gold, including the famous gold-foil rhinoceros.
Abandoned around 1290, it passed leadership north to Great Zimbabwe; today it is a UNESCO site and a national symbol of South Africa.
dyk: The golden rhinoceros of Mapungubwe, small enough to stand in the palm of a hand, was made of thin gold sheet fixed with tiny gold tacks onto a carved wooden core that has since decayed.
ev: Zhizo farmers at Schroda begin trading ivory with the coast
Leopard’s Kopje newcomers settle K2 (Bambandyanalo), which becomes the region’s main centre
The ruling elite moves onto Mapungubwe Hill, apart from the commoners below
The capital and its surroundings hold some 5,000 people
Mapungubwe Hill is abandoned and leadership passes north to Great Zimbabwe
The University of Pretoria begins excavations on Mapungubwe Hill
South Africa institutes the Order of Mapungubwe, its highest honour
The Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape becomes a UNESCO World Heritage Site

f.predecessor: K2 (Bambandyanalo), centre of the Leopard’s Kopje culture
